memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to order the house to be emptied before he goes in to examine the mould, so that nothing in the house will be pronounced unclean. After this the priest is to go in and inspect the house." - Lev 14:36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the priest steps inside, everything is carried out. Why? So that nothing in the house will be pronounced unclean.

This is a kindness. If the house is declared unclean while the family's possessions are still inside, they lose everything. Empty it first, and their belongings are safe.

God protects what can be saved before He examines what is wrong.

That is worth remembering when God begins to deal with something in our lives. His examination is never destructive for its own sake. He is careful. He knows exactly what needs to go and what should be preserved, and He does not confuse the two.

We are not so careful with each other. When we confront a problem in someone's life, we often damage far more than we needed to — the person's dignity, their confidence, their reputation. We knock the furniture about while dealing with the mould.

Paul gives us the better way: if someone is caught in a sin, you who live by the Spirit should restore that person gently (Gal 6:1). Gently. Restoration is the goal, and care is the method.

When God works on your house, He carries the furniture out first. Do the same for others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you damaged more than necessary when confronting someone?
2. What does God's carefulness tell you about how He deals with you?
3. Who needs gentle restoration from you rather than blunt correction?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are careful with me even when You confront what is wrong. Teach me to handle others with the same gentleness You have shown me. Amen.
